rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape [16, 16384] → size = 262144. Original condition: 262144 >= 4096 → TRUE. Mutant condition: 262144 >= 4097 → TRUE. Both conditions evaluate identically, selecting the same vectorized kernel path. The threshold difference (4096 vs 4097) only matters when size ∈ {4096} exactly, which is unreachable with fixed size 262144.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the threshold for selecting the vectorized kernel from 4096 to 4097. With the fixed input shape of [16, 16384], the total element count is 262144. Both the original condition (size >= 4096) and the mutated condition (size >= 4097) evaluate to TRUE for size=262144, causing both versions to execute identical code paths through elu_kernel_vectorized4. Since the same kernel with identical parameters is invoked in both cases, the outputs are bitwise identical regardless of input values. The mutation boundary at 4096/4097 elements is completely unreachable under the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects kernel selection at size boundary 4096-4097, but the fixed input size of 262144 always satisfies both conditions. No value-level variation can trigger a different execution path. The only way to kill this mutant would be to change the input shape to exactly 4096 elements, which violates the contract.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of kernel-selection thresholds, ensure the test suite includes inputs at each critical boundary (e.g., sizes 4095, 4096, 4097). When fixed-shape contracts prevent boundary testing, consider marking threshold mutations as equivalent under that specific contract, or design contracts that include boundary-hitting shapes.
